newsitem.title: USA: North Dakota wheat processing co-op raises $15 mln.
newsitem.headline: North Dakota wheat processing co-op raises $15 mln.

text.p: United Spring Wheat Processors, a wheat processing cooperative launched last year, said it raised more than $15 million in its first membership stock offering.
About 3,200 spring wheat producers from Minnesota, Montana, North Dakota and South Dakota invested $5,000 each in the venture, which will now formulate a business plan, USWP president Gary Lee said.
A plan to members is expected by the end of the year.
Each $5,000 commitment consisted of $200 in seed money for the start-up and $4,800 to be kept in an escrow account.

Interest from the escrow funds can be used for operations until a business plan is accepted by members, Lee said. When a business plan is accepted, members can choose to convert their money in escrow into equity in the cooperative.
"We have a strong membership base and are well on the way toward farmer ownership in the wheat products business," USWP chairman Mike Warner said.
The officials declined to comment on the kinds of spring wheat processing that might be included in the business plan.
